Terry McLaurin draws a plus matchup — IND concede 68 yds/game to WR1s (league ~58), and WAS funnel 23% of targets his way. A rec-yards spot.

The WAS host the IND as favorites of 1.5, with the total set at 48.5 — a market that implies a WAS 25–24 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 26% of its snaps with WAS in front, 39% within one score, and 34% with WAS chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 1.5 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.

The Key Matchups

WAS are soft against the run (143 yds/game allowed), and IND feed Jonathan Taylor a heavy 80% carry share — a rushing-yards spot.

Jayden Daniels adds rushing value — he scrambles on 6.7% of dropbacks, live for rush-yard and anytime-TD props.

Jayden Daniels has a passing-yards tailwind — IND allow 253 pass yds/game (vs ~230).

Chig Okonkwo has room to work — IND allow 42 yds/game to TE1s (vs ~35), a receiving-yards and target angle.

Alec Pierce draws a plus matchup — WAS concede 68 yds/game to WR1s (league ~58). A rec-yards spot.

Touchdown Board

Jonathan Taylor is a bell-cow (80% of carries) meeting a defense that allows 0.81 RB rushing TDs/game — strong anytime-TD equity.

Tyler Warren is a live anytime-TD dart — WAS are leaky to tight ends in the end zone (0.35 TE TDs/game vs ~0.24).

Alec Pierce carries TD equity — WAS surrender 0.51 WR1 receiving scores a game.

WAS — a run-heavy offense

WAS are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 38% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

Jacory Croskey-Merritt (11 carries, 48 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Terry McLaurin projects for 6 targets and 51 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Chig Okonkwo (TE, 4 targets, 33 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

IND — a balanced offense

IND are a balanced offense — their run/pass split by game state tracks the league closely (44% pass when leading vs 44% average), so their players' usage is driven more by role than by any strong situational lean.

Jonathan Taylor (16 carries, 78 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Alec Pierce projects for 5 targets and 51 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Tyler Warren (TE, 6 targets, 47 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 2-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.

This preview and the projections below regenerate through the week as injuries, weather and line moves update the inputs.
